recipes.title: David's Roku + Denon Setup
recipes.summary: David's working Clonker configuration: Denon-centric Den and Roku-centric Sunroom, with an unused third room.
description: This complete Config v5 recipe is based on a working configuration exported from the physical Clonker.
Room 1, Den, uses Roku for navigation and playback, with a Denon receiver handling volume and mute. Movie, Music, and Vinyl Custom Actions invoke Denon Quick Select presets.

Room 2, Sunroom, uses Roku for navigation, playback, volume, and mute, controlling the Denon AVR volume through HDMI CEC. This also demonstrates the Roku volume command approach applicable to compatible Roku smart TVs.
The recipe includes explicitly typed devices, protocol-aware commands, stable Custom Action identifiers, and an unconfigured third room.

Download the JSON file and import it through the Clonker configuration editor. Review and customize all device endpoints and commands before explicitly saving. IP addresses are not automatically substituted.
rooms: Room 1 -- Den: Roku navigation, Denon volume/mute, four Custom Actions
Room 2 -- Sunroom: Roku navigation, Roku volume/mute, three Custom Actions
Room 3 -- Present but unconfigured; available for future expansion
custom_actions: Den: Movie → Roku Home, wait 3 seconds, Denon Quick Select 1
Den: Music → Roku Home, wait 3 seconds, Denon Quick Select 2
Den: Vinyl → Roku Home, wait 3 seconds, Denon Quick Select 3
Den: Audio Cycle → Cycle Denon Movie listening modes
Sunroom: Movie → Roku Home, wait 3 seconds, Denon Quick Select 1
Sunroom: Music → Roku Home, wait 3 seconds, Denon Quick Select 2
Sunroom: Audio Cycle → Cycle Denon Movie listening modes

recipes.title: David's LG webOS Starter
recipes.summary: David's LG G1 OLED configuration, demonstrating native LG webOS SSAP and pointer commands in a single-room setup.
description: This complete Config v5 recipe was created for Chapter 13 of the Clonker project: The Monster Learns Another Language.
Room 1, Sunroom, contains a single configured LG webOS television. Volume and mute use SSAP commands, while navigation, Select, Back, and Home use pointer commands.
The recipe demonstrates structured JSON payloads, independent mute ON/OFF commands, and Custom Actions combining SSAP and pointer commands.
Power and media transport controls are intentionally unassigned during initial integration testing.
A valid LG webOS client key must be supplied manually through the Clonker configuration editor. The published recipe contains only a placeholder credential.
Operational compatibility is pending Chapter 13 firmware integration and testing. Review the device endpoint and authentication settings before explicitly saving.
rooms: Room 1 -- Sunroom: LG G1 OLED, native webOS navigation, volume/mute, three Custom Actions
custom_actions: Sunroom: Get Volume → Request current volume using SSAP
Sunroom: Launch Home → Launch the LG Home application using SSAP
Sunroom: Home & Right → Launch LG Home, wait 1.5 seconds, send pointer RIGHT
